profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer — Frontend | React · TypeScript · Next.js
profile.summary:
I'm now the sole engineer of the ICP Dashboard (dashboard.internetcomputer.org), the Internet Computer's primary public explorer and analytics platform: a React, TypeScript, and Next.js web application with 70+ pages and over a million visits a year. I own the frontend end to end. This year I also took over its 5 backend API services, written in Rust and Python, both new to me. Working with Claude, I converted 20+ hours of handover meetings into per-repo documentation and have shipped multiple production backend releases since. Before that I was the product's tech lead, leading a team of 5 engineers and a designer through its ground-up redesign, 11 months from concept to launch. DFINITY recruited me off my own open-source explorer.

My stack is React, Next.js, and TypeScript/JavaScript, plus TanStack Query (React Query), Jest, and React Testing Library. I care about the quality bar as much as the features: while leading the team I reviewed the majority of frontend pull requests, promoted shared components to reduce duplication, and pushed testing adoption to 2,200+ tests. Behind the frontend work is a deep systems background: 40+ product modules in C++ and C# for enterprise print production software, including printer protocols implemented down to the TCP/IP socket level.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer (Frontend) / Tech Lead
positions.description:
As sole engineer since April 2026, I own the ICP Dashboard (dashboard.internetcomputer.org, 70+ pages, 1M+ visits per year): the React/TypeScript/Next.js frontend end to end, plus its 5 backend API services in Rust and Python, taken over this year, AI-assisted. I'm currently shipping ICP Dashboard 7.0.0 (July 2026), which applies the network's new branding across every surface.

Before that I was the product's Tech Lead, leading a team of 5 engineers and a designer through a ground-up redesign, delivered in 11 months from concept to launch. I gathered and synthesized feedback from 50+ contributors spanning DFINITY teams, leadership, and the community into the roadmap that became the redesign's North Star, and convened experts from 5 platform teams to define the network-health metrics that shipped on the redesigned dashboard.

I built the redesign's signature feature, the rotating 3D Earth that opens the app, along with analytics for the Bitcoin integration and chain-key tokens (BTC, ETH, USDC) and the Tokenomics Analyzer, which makes complex DAO tokenomics understandable. Throughout, I held the frontend quality bar: code review, shared components, and React Testing Library adoption, with the suite now at 2,200+ tests.
positions.insights: Leading Development Teams, React.js and +11 skills

positions.title: Frontend Lead (part-time contract)
positions.description:
DFINITY recruited me on the strength of my open-source ICP Explorer to serve as sole frontend developer of the official ICP Dashboard (dashboard.internetcomputer.org). I grew it from a one-page stats app into a full product, and was hired full-time in 2023.

I delivered the transaction explorer required for the token's Coinbase listing; the live Voting Results view, later adopted across other Internet Computer products; and the Canister page, an auto-generated UI for calling any smart contract on the network. I also migrated the production app to Next.js single-handedly for better performance and SEO.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer / Software Architect
positions.locationName: Palo Alto, California, United States · On-site
positions.description:
My career there centered on Solimar Print Director Enterprise, an output management platform that receives print jobs from host systems, converts them between formats, and routes them to production printers. I shipped major projects solo, taking on technologies no one at the company knew, learning from thousands of pages of specs: zero knowledge on day one, expert level by release.

I designed and built 40+ product modules in C++ and C#, spanning document conversion pipelines (PDF, PostScript, AFPDS), printer and host connectivity, and configuration UIs. I architected a reusable print-language conversion system shared by multiple product modules; a bug fixed in one conversion component was fixed in every module built on it.

I implemented printer protocols down to the socket level: IPDS over a proprietary TCP/IP transport that was never publicly documented; IPP (binary over HTTP) on a C++ HTTP server written from scratch; and JDF (XML over HTTP).

positions.title: Creator
positions.description: I created ICP Explorer (icpexplorer.org), an open-source block explorer for the Internet Computer, built in React. I started it in 2018, before the network existed, using simulated data, and it went live on DFINITY's public APIs in early 2021.

volunteerExperiences.description: Taught iOS programming to kids and adults in East Palo Alto.
